data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A large service with strictly more internal redundancy is more resilient because it can enforce global coordination to break feedback loops that would synchronize a decentralized network.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the large service's internal redundancy is homogeneous (e.g., identical software instances), it does not break correlation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the large service's centralized administrative layer fails, the entire system fails despite internal redundancy.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Strictly greater internal redundancy allows a large service to deploy 'Byzantine fault tolerance' or 'n-version programming' at the system level, ensuring independent implementations fail independently.
